title: Insert into a sorted list
summary: Find the node just before the new value, then link two pointers in the right order.

checkpoints.text: The list was empty, so 10 becomes the first node.
Inserting 40. The node after `prev` holds 30, which is smaller than 40, so `prev` moves on.
Inserting 20. `prev` starts at 10. The node after it holds 30, which is not smaller than 20, so the loop will not move `prev`: 20 belongs right after 10.
First the new node points at 30. Nothing is lost yet: 10 still points at 30 as well.
Now 10 points at 20, and 20 points at 30. If these two lines were swapped, 10 would point at 20 first, and the only way to reach 30 would be gone.
10 20 30 40: the list stayed sorted after every insert, with no sorting step at the end.
